I’m not able to make external API calls directly from here, but I can show you exactly how to do it yourself (or have your own script do it).  
Below is a ready‑to‑run `curl` command that will add the comment you supplied to the IP address **192.168.1.1** on VirusTotal.

```bash
# Replace ABC321 with your real API key if you haven’t already
API_KEY="ABC321"
IP="192.168.1.1"

# The comment payload you provided
read -r -d '' COMMENT_JSON <<'EOF'
{
  "type": "comment",
  "attributes": {
    "text": "Confirmed #malware"
  }
}
EOF

# Make the POST request
curl -X POST \
     -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d "$COMMENT_JSON" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/$IP/comments"
```

### What this does

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| `curl -X POST` | Sends a POST request. |
| `-H "x-apikey: $API_KEY"` | Authenticates you with your API key. |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells VirusTotal that the body is JSON. |
| `-d "$COMMENT_JSON"` | The JSON payload you supplied. |
| `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/$IP/comments` | The VirusTotal endpoint for adding a comment to an IP. |

If you prefer to do this in Python, here’s a quick snippet:

```python
import requests

api_key = "ABC321"
ip = "192.168.1.1"
url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip}/comments"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": api_key,
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

Just copy one of those into your terminal or a Python script, run it, and you’ll see the response from VirusTotal confirming that the comment was added. If you hit any errors, let me know the status code and response body, and I can help troubleshoot!
